item.title: 8918 reproducciones · 32 reacciones | U.S. envoy Jeff Bartos was spotted reading an anti-Castro book, “The Double Life of Fidel Castro,” during an address by Cuban Foreign Minister Bruno Rodríguez at the United Nations General Assembly on Wednesday. It comes a day after U.S. ambassador to the U.N. Michael Waltz had a public confrontation with Cuba’s ambassador to the U.N., Ernesto Soberón, during the annual U.N. vote on a resolution calling for an end to the U.S. embargo on Cuba. The two engaged in a tense exchange, with Soberón calling Waltz “a liar.” Tensions between the two countries are mounting ahead of the vote on the non-binding resolution, which has been adopted by the U.N. General Assembly by wide margins every year since 1992. This year’s vote comes amid heightened tensions over U.S. restrictions on oil supplies to Cuba. | CBS News

item.title: Fuel costs jump from $1,800 to $8,000: Cruise ship residents forced ashore in Cambodia
item.description: Cruise ship Villa Vie Odyssey had to disembark its passengers in Cambodia due to soaring fuel expenses. The ship had operated for over two years, accommodating long-term residents on board. As fuel costs increased significantly, the company announced the suspension of operations. Passengers were provided with temporary accommodation while some already departed for their destinations. The ship is expected to refuel before continuing its journey after leaving Cambodia. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: ¿Por qué la Fiscalía de Perú archivó el caso de esterilizaciones forzadas pese a reconocerlo?
item.description: Durante décadas, miles de mujeres, en su mayoría indígenas y campesinas, buscaron justicia por las esterilizaciones forzadas realizadas durante el gobierno de Alberto Fujimori. Aunque la Fiscalía de Perú reconoció que muchas intervenciones se realizaron sin consentimiento libre e informado, decidió archivar la investigación. ¿Por qué? item.title: Así fue la 'ruta de escape' de Flávio Bolsonaro desde Brasil hacia Estados Unidos
item.description: Tras abandonar Brasil en medio de la controversia por las investigaciones judiciales que enfrenta, Flávio Bolsonaro emprendió un recorrido que lo llevó primero a Argentina, luego a Ecuador y finalmente a Estados Unidos. Durante la madrugada del miércoles, el avión privado en el que viajaba realizó una escala técnica en Guayaquil para repostar combustible antes de continuar su trayecto hacia Miami, donde llegó junto a su familia. Horas después de su llegada a territorio estadounidense, Bolsonaro se proclamó "líder de Brasil". Fuente: France 24 - Español.

item.title: Regulatory tightening in Hong Kong sees delistings outnumber resumptions: report
item.description: The tightening of Hong Kong’s securities regulations – in the wake of property developer Evergrande’s liquidation and unrelated IPO frauds – has resulted in more delistings than resumptions for the first time in three years, according to a report by accountants Grant Thornton. Hong Kong saw 35 delistings in the 12 months to August this year but only 21 resumptions, the report said. “Regulators have comprehensively tightened resumption requirements,” said Barry Tong, national leader of forensic...
